and the counting tasks of Section 4 isolate whether a model can keep track of objects that leave the frame and come back. The suite extends both lines of work from still images to short clips and to questions whose answer requires combining what was seen at different moments.

**Answer formats.** Most clip suites ask multiple-choice questions, which a model can sometimes answer by eliminating implausible options without watching the clip. We keep a multiple-choice version for comparison but report the free-form version as the main result (Section 5.3).

**Human baselines.** Twelve volunteers answered a random tenth of the items under the same time limit as the models, which gives a reference point for how hard each category is for people who see the clip once.

## B SUITE DETAILS

Below we give the suite's size per category first, then the writing guide that annotators followed, and last the rules by which results are grouped for reporting.

### B.1 SIZE PER CATEGORY

Table 4 lists the number of items per category and the length of their clips; Figure 6 breaks the same items down by setting. The categories are deliberately uneven in size, because some kinds of question are much harder to write well; the smallest has 41 items and the largest 212.
